body.x: Betterial (CEO Yoo Kwanghyun) will attend CES 2025 in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10. The company will present its innovative carbon nanotube (CNT) dispersion technology for electric vehicle (EV) batteries at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Founded in 2018 with the vision of “Better Material for a Better Future,” Betterial specializes in developing and commercializing CNT conductive dispersions for secondary batteries. The company has created over ten CNT dispersion products, addressing markets ranging from EVs and energy storage systems (ESS) to small batteries. It has secured more than 40 patents, underscoring its strong technical capabilities.

Betterial’s CNT dispersion technology overcomes the challenge of CNTs clumping together, enabling the production of high-quality CNT dispersions. With an annual production capacity of over 1,000 tons, the company offers products that balance superior performance with cost competitiveness. CNT dispersions are also recognized for significantly improving battery performance, especially as a doping material for next-generation silicon anodes.

At CES 2025, Betterial will highlight its advanced dispersion technology that ensures uniform CNT integration with battery components. The company’s proprietary technology enhances the functionality of CNT-SiOx composite anodes, boosting conductivity and electrode performance through consistent coating on silicon oxide surfaces.

Betterial’s products, specifically designed for EV batteries, deliver up to 70% increases in energy density and charging cycles. They also support ultra-fast charging, enabling high-capacity batteries to charge in 10 minutes.

“Leading domestic and international battery manufacturers have recognized Our CNT dispersion technology, and we’ve strengthened partnerships, including collaborations with POSCO,” a Betterial representative noted. “We’re thrilled to bring this innovation to CES, the world’s largest tech exhibition, as a step toward expanding our global presence.”

The company has also established strong partnerships with battery leaders in regions like the UK, the US, Germany, Israel, and Canada. “We aim to use CES as a launchpad for expanding into North American and European markets,” the representative added. “Leveraging connections made at the event, we plan to engage with potential clients, conduct product tests, secure market approvals, and steadily increase our delivery outcomes.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally.
